title: Explainable AI spatial features estimate residual cancer burden in breast cancer
summary: Deep learning segmented tumor, necrosis and lymphocytes on H&E patches and 11 spatial features were built. In 347 post-neoadjuvant patients (182 development, 165 external), XGBoost reached external AUC 0.781, 0.896 and 1.000 for the three RCB tasks, with TCGA-BRCA (843 cases) exploratory. The AUC of 1.000 reflects complete separation and may reflect few events.
ai_technology: Deep learning segmentation (VGG-16), multiple instance learning and XGBoost with SHAP and Grad-CAM

evidence.tested: Second-center external validation (n=165) and exploratory TCGA-BRCA analysis.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance and clinical benefit are not reported; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Segmented tissue compartments and modeled residual cancer burden.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
